title.en: A Job That Still Isn't Enough

A2.text: Meet a typical student here. She studies in the day and delivers food at night. She works hard every week, but her bank account never grows.
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), drafted directly (Gemini quota exhausted for this session)
A2.basis: New mission, no workbook source; written per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md, angle distinct from sdg1 (general safety-net framing) and sdg1-3 (education/mobility framing): the labor market specifically. Facts and sources: minimum wage NT$29,500/month, NT$196/hour from 1 Jan 2026 (up from NT$28,590/NT$190 in 2025), 10th consecutive annual rise, cumulative +47.4% monthly/+63.3% hourly, 2.47 million workers benefiting (Ministry of Labor announcements via Taiwan News/Focus Taiwan, Sep-Dec 2025). OECD low-wage threshold ~NT$390,000/year; 1.26 million full-time employees (16.8%) below it in 2024; median regular monthly wage ~NT$37,000 (DGBAS 2024 wage statistics via Liberty Times). Atypical (part-time/temporary/dispatch) employment over 800,000 workers in 2024 (DGBAS Manpower Utilization Survey via 人間福報). Delivery riders ~88,000 by end of 2020, historically classified as contractors excluded from the Labor Standards Act; 2019 rider deaths triggered union push (Rest of World, New Bloom Magazine, GBLL). Delivery Workers Rights Protection and Delivery Platform Management Act: passed by Legislative Yuan 6 Jan 2026, promulgated 21 Jan 2026, effective 21 Jul 2026; NT$45/order floor rising with minimum wage, mandatory group accident insurance and liability insurance, deactivation appeal process (Legislative Yuan, Ministry of Labor, CNA, Taipei Times, Jul 2026). Rev.2: trimmed word counts that exceeded the 20-second cap (comma-formatted figures like NT$29,500 tokenize as multiple spoken words), and simplified vocabulary that pushed long-word% above the A2 band.
